Retimed Bellman Flows Escaping the impossible triangle of velocity bootstrapping

A flow critic for distributional reinforcement learning that reads its successor teacher on a slower clock. The retimed query keeps the Gaussian start, links every training point to the teacher in closed form, and gives a conditionally unbiased velocity target with no new hyperparameter.

Boyang Xu, Shengzhe Chen, Hao Yan

Arizona State University

Preprint, September 2026. Builds on Path-Coupled Bellman Flows (ICML 2026).

Read the paper See the code Cite

Bootstrapping a velocity is a matching problem

A flow critic represents the law of a return, not only its mean, by a velocity field that transports Gaussian noise to returns. Training it by temporal-difference learning creates a mismatch, however: flow matching learns a whole trajectory over flow time t∈[0,1]t \in [0,1]t∈[0,1], whereas the distributional Bellman equation constrains only the endpoint at t=1t = 1t=1.

Velocity bootstrapping addresses this mismatch in the way bootstrapping does for scalar values. The student regresses its velocity onto a target built from a frozen teacher's velocity at the successor state–action pair, rather than onto a noisy sampled return. Consequently, the quality of the target depends on how each point of the student's path is matched to a point on the teacher's path. On the source-consistent straight path, the student point and its velocity are

Xt=(1−t) X0+t (R+γ~X1′),Y=X˙t=R+γ~X1′−X0,X_t = (1-t)\,X_0 + t\,(R + \tilde\gamma X'_1), \qquad Y = \dot X_t = R + \tilde\gamma X'_1 - X_0,Xt​=(1−t)X0​+t(R+γ~​X1′​),Y=X˙t​=R+γ~​X1′​−X0​,

where X0∼N(0,1)X_0 \sim \mathcal N(0,1)X0​∼N(0,1) is the source, X1′X'_1X1′​ the successor return and γ~\tilde\gammaγ~​ the actual Bellman multiplier of the backup. A good match should have three properties.

SSource consistency
The student path starts from standard Gaussian noise at t=0t = 0t=0, the same source the critic uses when it generates returns.
AAffinity
Every student point is an affine image of one teacher point, so the teacher query follows from the student point in closed form for every noise coupling.
DDecoupled generation
The successor return is generated from fresh noise, independent of the student's source, which is how the reused critic was itself trained.

With a coupling-matched teacher and exact population regression, affinity and decoupled generation together make the bootstrapped target unbiased on canonical fields.

Why no same-time design gets all three

After removing tRtRtR, the student point weights the source and the successor endpoint as (1−t, γ~t)(1-t,\ \tilde\gamma t)(1−t, γ~​t), whereas the teacher's chord read at the same time weights them as (1−t, t)(1-t,\ t)(1−t, t). No scale that depends only on ttt and γ~\tilde\gammaγ~​ can reconcile the two for every endpoint pair unless γ~=1\tilde\gamma = 1γ~​=1; this is the impossible triangle of Corollary 3.1. Value Flows keeps the affine link but starts from a shifted source, and PCBF keeps the Gaussian source but leaves a residual in X0X_0X0​ and shares the noise. ReBF escapes the triangle by reading the chord at an earlier time instead.

Why closing it matters

Return laws, not just means

Across three exact reward processes, a 16-dimensional successor-feature task and an OGBench maze, ReBF has the lowest Wasserstein error in every setting, up to 7.7× lower than PCBF.

See the accuracy results

No new knob to tune

The retimed clock is fixed by the discount and the flow time. Full correction is the best retimed setting in every environment and data split, whereas the best same-time setting drifts toward no correction at all.

Explore the design space

Long-horizon control

On 38 offline RL tasks, ReBF has the highest domain average on cube-double, scene and puzzle-4x4, the long-horizon manipulation domains where target bias compounds over many backups.

Read the teacher on a slower clock

ReBF keeps the source-consistent straight path and changes only when the teacher is read. Rewriting the student point as an affine image of the successor chord forces a warped clock: the teacher is queried at τ(t)≤t\tau(t) \le tτ(t)≤t, and the scale α(t)\alpha(t)α(t) and the query point ξt\xi_tξt​ follow in closed form.

  1. Keep the straight source path

    The student path starts at the Gaussian source and ends at the Bellman sample, exactly as in PCBF, which gives property (S).

    Xt=(1−t) X0+t (R+γ~X1′)X_t = (1-t)\,X_0 + t\,(R + \tilde\gamma X'_1)Xt​=(1−t)X0​+t(R+γ~​X1′​)

  2. Retime the teacher query

What the analysis guarantees

The analysis shows that the retimed clock is not one choice among many but the only affine lift that commutes with the Bellman map, and that together with fresh noise it makes the target unbiased and the training operator a contraction.

The impossible triangleCorollary 3.1

For 0<γ~<10 < \tilde\gamma < 10<γ~​<1 and 0<t<10 < t < 10<t<1, no scale α(t)\alpha(t)α(t) depending only on (t,γ~)(t, \tilde\gamma)(t,γ~​) makes the same-time identity hold for every endpoint pair while XtX_tXt​ stays the straight source path.

Full correction is optimal for an exact teacherProposition 5

The correction weight trades the residual bridge noise SSS carried by the sampled chord against the teacher error eee, so κ=1\kappa = 1κ=1 is the risk minimiser exactly when the teacher is exact.

κ⋆=SS+∥e∥2\kappa^\star = \frac{S}{S + \|e\|^2}κ⋆=S+∥e∥2S​
Why shared noise plateausProposition A.1

With shared noise, a coupling-matched teacher would return the sampled chord exactly. The reused critic is that teacher only if its trajectories are straight lines traversed at constant speed, which flow-matching trajectories generally are not, so a self-teaching critic with shared noise keeps feeding bias into the backup. Independent noise removes the mismatch, because the required teacher is then the marginal field the critic already learns.

Results

The experiments ask three questions: does ReBF learn more accurate return laws, do retiming and decoupled noise together explain the gain, and do better laws translate into control?

It recovers return laws more accurately

The accuracy benchmark uses three Markov reward processes with exactly known return laws (Bernoulli, Solitaire and a Discrete Monte Carlo chain), a four-rooms task with 16-dimensional successor features, and the OGBench pointmaze-teleport maze scored against Monte Carlo rollouts.

Retiming and decoupled noise are both needed

All arms share one implementation with three switches: the clock, the noise coupling ρ1\rho_1ρ1​ and the correction weight κ\kappaκ. Neither switch helps alone. Retiming lowers the error only with independent noise, because under shared noise a scalar chord is recoverable from either query and both clocks chase the same biased target; conversely, a same-time clock with independent noise keeps a residual.

Full correction is the retimed optimum

Tuning κ\kappaκ separately for each family on five seeds and scoring on five held-out seeds shows where each optimum sits. The best retimed weight is 1 in every environment and split, as Theorem 5.3 predicts, whereas the best same-time weight is never 1 and moves toward the uncorrected critic.

More readout steps keep paying off

Reading the same trained critics out with more Euler steps measures the field itself rather than the solver. From 10 to 200 steps, ReBF improves by a factor of two to four in every environment, whereas PCBF with full correction improves by 1.3–2.1× and then levels off: a biased field is not rescued by integrating it more accurately.

It holds up on 38 offline RL tasks

The control benchmark covers four state-based OGBench domains, two pixel-based OGBench domains and eight D4RL Adroit tasks. Scores average eight seeds, or four for pixel-based tasks, and baselines span quantile critics, flow critics and strong scalar methods.

Limitations

The analysis concerns policy evaluation on small Markov reward processes under a fixed policy, so the offline RL scores are not a test of the theory, and how a flow critic should be used to extract a better policy remains open. Several results are proved only in a correlated-Gaussian model, and convergence is established on canonical fields with independent generation; uniqueness and convergence of the self-consistent training map from arbitrary initial fields, or under coupled generation, are not.

Implementation

The OGBench agent is written in JAX and reuses the actor, return-flow networks, target updates and policy extraction of the PCBF implementation. Only the critic target changes, along three independent switches. The excerpt below is the core of that target.

Critic target, condensed
# Successor seed: rho = 1 shares the student's noise; rho = 0 is fresh (ReBF).
path_noises = jax.random.normal(path_rng, (batch_size, 1))      # X0
aux_noises = jax.random.normal(aux_rng, (batch_size, 1))        # E
successor_noises = rho * path_noises + jnp.sqrt(1 - rho**2) * aux_noises
times = jax.random.uniform(time_rng, (batch_size, 1))

# Successor endpoint X'1 from the target flow; straight student path.
next_returns = compute_flow_returns(successor_noises, next_obs, next_act)
endpoint = rewards + gamma_tilde * next_returns
noisy_returns = (1 - times) * path_noises + times * endpoint    # X_t
bcfm_target = endpoint - path_noises                            # Y
sample_velocity = next_returns - path_noises                    # C

if query == "retimed":                                          # ReBF
    alpha = jnp.maximum(1 - (1 - gamma_tilde) * times, 1e-6)
    query_times = gamma_tilde * times / alpha                   # tau(t)
    gain = gamma_tilde / alpha                                  # g(t)
else:                                                           # PCBF
    query_times, gain = times, gamma_tilde
query_returns = (1 - query_times) * path_noises \
              + query_times * next_returns                      # xi_t

teacher = target_critic_flow(query_returns, query_times, next_obs, next_act)
target = jax.lax.stop_gradient(
    bcfm_target + kappa * gain * (teacher - sample_velocity))
